THEATRE REVIEW THE CEZANNE SYNDROME

Friday, June 15, 1990

ROBERT CUSHMAN

Written by Normand Canac-Marquis Translated by Louison Danis Directed by Jim Millan Starring John Jarvis, Martha Burns and George Merner At the Brigantine Room, Toronto Onstage car repairs notwithstanding, some things are just plain mystifying Now, is that Cezanne or Suzanne? BY ROBERT CUSHMAN Special to The Globe and Mail THE Cezanne Syndrome opened at the World Stage festival at Toronto's Harborfront on Wednesday, three years after receiving its world premiere in Montreal. In the meantime, it has been seen in Ottawa, Chicago, Vancouver and New York. In each city, it received reviews that the Toronto producers have been happy to flourish in their handouts. It is a horrible thought, but maybe there should be a theatrical Meech Lake, charged to expedite the progress of important Canadian plays to the city that fancies itself Canada's theatrical capital.
